patch_description: This replaces the Kalman/RTS pipeline with a fundamentally different paradigm: multiscale zero-phase Savitzky-Golay (local polynomial) smoothing with an adaptive degree and window, plus a velocity-clamped trend reconciliation pass. Savitzky-Golay fits low-order polynomials in sliding windows via fixed FIR coefficients, giving exact zero phase delay (no lag) while preserving polynomial trends (high tracking accuracy by construction). A robust noise scale is estimated via MAD of first differences, and the SG window/degree is chosen adaptively per-signal. A second coarser SG pass provides the "slow trend" reference, and the output is clamped toward consistent per-step displacement relative to that trend, suppressing spurious slope reversals and false reversals while keeping genuine dynamics (the clamp is soft and correlation-guarded). Final light bilateral one-pole pass damps residual ripple. All operations are linear-time convolutions (fast, vectorized) — better efficiency than the per-sample Kalman loops. Output contract preserved: y[i] ↔ input time i+window_size-1, len = n-window_size+1.
